target_customer: EV drivers, rideshare drivers and fleets (Rivian, Hertz and the City of San Francisco later cited as customers)
problem: EV charging payment is fragmented across many networks and apps, and fleets lack expense management for charging. Bluedot offers one card and app with a flat rate and cash back.
business_model: Fintech card interchange and charging margin, later fleet charging management software
product_category: EV charging payments and fleet expense platform

founders.name: Ferhat Babacan
education: Munich Technical University, master's program (dropped out)
founders.background_notes: Source: YC company page. Operated 100 plus EV charging stations per the YC description and was a national volleyball player in Turkey.

founders.name: Selinay Parlak
founders.background_notes: Source: YC page and TechCrunch. Worked on multiple EV projects, named a Business Insider Rising Star in the EV industry. High school friend of Babacan.

exit.reason: Epic acquired Bluedot's brand, platform technology, intellectual property, customer contracts and key team; the price was not disclosed.

technical_complexity.rationale: Issuing a debit card through a bank partner and integrating with multiple charging networks (access to about 60% of US stations at launch) took fintech and integration work but was standard engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Network access deals and rewards are copyable, and charging networks could add their own payments. Partnerships with dealers and fleets gave some distribution.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Charging networks built their own apps and plug-and-charge. Bluedot was ultimately acquired by Epic Charging in May 2026 rather than copied out of existence.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in January 2023 described founders citing charging station utilization of 5 to 8 percent and fragmented payment across networks. The company reported at YC about 40 to 45 percent weekly growth and $110K weekly GMV, per the YC long description (company claim).

identity.logo: White logo image, design not described by sources
identity.voice_and_tone: Upbeat, friendly and direct, speaks to the reader as you with short punchy headlines about savings and convenience

branding.brand_signature: Free Charging Day, a monthly random day the company covers a card member's public charging
branding.community_and_virality: EV forum threads (Rivian, F-150 Lightning) discuss the card and Free Charging Day, one user saying the promotion may have stopped. TechCrunch and MarketWatch covered the launch in early 2023.

brand_strength.rationale: Early TechCrunch and MarketWatch coverage and forum discussion by EV owners, but a generic name and a niche audience. Epic Charging says Bluedot will remain a separate brand.

pivots.from: Debit card and app for individual EV owners and rideshare drivers
pivots.to: Fleet charging payment and management platform
pivots.why: TechCrunch in January 2023 said it planned to target fleets next; later coverage names fleet customers such as Rivian and Hertz. Not described as a formal pivot.

outcome_analysis: Bluedot started with a debit card for EV drivers, then moved toward fleets, and raised more than $5 million total from strategic backers including Porsche, Ford and Axel Springer. Epic Charging acquired its brand, technology and team on May 1, 2026 at an undisclosed price, giving access to over 80 percent of US public charging ports. That looks like a modest outcome with no disclosed return; the founders' automotive background fit the EV timing.
notes: YC directory lists status Active, but Pulse 2 (article dated May 12, 2026) reports Epic Charging completed the acquisition on May 1, 2026 and Bluedot continues as a separate brand; the company site still shows no acquisition notice. Total funding is described as more than $5M by Pulse 2 and an EV Report headline says $5M; the round breakdown after the $2M pre-seed is not sourced, so it is not recorded and coverage is partial. Craft.co lists $7M, unverified. The pre-seed date uses the TechCrunch article date as the report said recently closed. The YC page says founded 2021 and a launch of the Bluedot card on December 14, 2022. Competition list is empty because TechCrunch named no competitors and the competitor pages found were low-authority aggregators.
